meta.precision: float32 (TF32 off), A100 GPUs, early exit after 3 loops on the solution
meta.subtitle: Each pixel is one starting thought for the same Sudoku. Colour is how many loops the model took to settle on its answer.
limits: One puzzle, one model. EqR's released Sudoku checkpoint on a rating-47 puzzle, the one behind loopscape's own figure. Other puzzles give other maps.

One slice. A random 2-D plane (seed 0) through the all-zero starting state of a 49,664-dimensional space. The starting thoughts here are tiny (distance from zero at most 1.41) next to EqR's usual random start (about 223).

Almost every start ends right. 99.9% of the 4,194,304 starts of the full map reach the true solution. What is fractal is how long it takes. The 3,441 pixels that do not end on the solution are drawn in amber: 3,441 are starts still changing at loop 24 (UNSETTLED), 0 settled on a wrong grid (STUCK).

float32 is touchy. Re-run on a second float32 implementation, 97% of the pixels with flat surroundings keep their settle time but only 26% of the speckle pixels do. On the same GPU, a nudge of 1e-6 to a start leaves 97% of flat-region pixels unchanged and 18% of speckle pixels. (Ours vs loopscape's published image: 64.4% of 62,500 pixels identical.) TF32 or bfloat16 give a different picture. Read single speckle pixels as one realisation; the structure is the result.

The complexity thins out when you zoom. In 5×5-pixel boxes, 69% touch a boundary at the full map's pixel pitch (1e-03), but only 31% in the layer magnified ×128 (pitch 3e-05). Zoom beyond ×128 was not rendered: a trial window at ×5,120 held only speckle next to a flat domain.
Settle time is measured over 24 loops with the model's noise switched off, as in loopscape: the loop after which the decoded grid never changes again.
how: EqR checkpoint (locuslab) run as in loopscape: z_H = a·u + b·v, z_L = 0, 24 loops, noise off, float32.
6,016,804 starting thoughts computed on A100 GPUs of the ALICE cluster (Leiden): 2048² for the full plane and 5 zoom layers around the marked point. About 25 A100-hours.
A start stops being computed once its decoded grid has equalled the true solution for 3 loops in a row (checked against full 24-loop runs).
Reproduction check: loopscape's published 1000×1000 image, every 4th pixel: basin entropy 1.416 vs 1.412, boundary dimension 1.873 vs 1.872.
